articles.headlineJa: ファンタジー・フットボール対戦ランキング：第4週はタイラー・ウォーレンとテタイロア・マクミランを評価上方修正
articles.descriptionJa: 今週のNFLの試合における、ファンタジーフットボールの主要4ポジションでの最も有利な対戦と最も不利な対戦を紹介。
articles.body:
Making tough lineup decisions each week can be the most challenging part of fantasy football. When you're torn between two similar players, start the player with the superior matchup.

But exactly how does one determine the best (and worst) weekly matchups?

The matchup rankings provide a schedule-independent method to evaluate positional matchups, ranking all 32 opposing defenses in order of most to least favorable for opposing players at all four skill positions. Instead of relying upon seasonal totals, we calibrate points-allowed data to show how each defense fared relative to the difficulty of the schedule it has faced. 

For Week 4, 2026 full-season data is used, but once five weeks are in the books, only the most recent five weeks' numbers will be used.

"Adj. FPA," or Adjusted Fantasy Points Allowed, reflects how far above or below players' weekly PPR fantasy point averages that defense held opponents at that position. A positive number means that the matchup is favorable; a negative number means it is unfavorable.

Finally, a caveat: Matchups are only one ingredient in my rankings formula. Not every favorable matchup should be exploited, nor unfavorable matchup avoided. If you want the most complete source for whom to start, consult our weekly rankings.

Quarterbacks

Matchups highlight: Jared Goff, Detroit Lions (at Carolina Panthers, Sunday Night Football). One the more quietly reliable quarterbacks, Goff joins Josh Allen, Brock Purdy and Tyler Shough among four with at least 16 fantasy points in each of the season's first three weeks. Of those four, he's the only one who hasn't been intercepted. Goff next faces the Panthers defense, which, aside from their 24-point Week 2 against the Atlanta Falcons third- and fourth-string quarterbacks, has been beaten up by the position. Caleb Williams (Week 1) and Deshaun Watson (Week 3) combined averaged 0.59 fantasy points per passing attempt -- the league average is 0.45 -- against the Panthers.

Others to like:

Trevor Lawrence, Jacksonville Jaguars (at Cincinnati Bengals)

Bryce Young, Panthers (at Lions, SNF)

Matchup to avoid: Jalen Hurts, Philadelphia Eagles (vs. Los Angeles Rams). He's off to a so-so start despite facing a favorable September schedule (WSH, @TEN, @CHI), due to inconsistent protection -- the Eagles rank 22nd in pass block win rate -- and a running game that hasn't fully launched (13th-ranked 110.7 yards per game, 19th-ranked 9.2% explosive run rate). That's of concern when Hurts faces the Rams, who rank second in yards allowed per passing attempt (5.2) and ninth in Total QBR allowed (53.2). Hurts' mobility presents his best case for a top-10 positional ranking this week, but aim to do better from that lineup slot.

articles.headline: Man City to appeal guilty verdict in Premier League breaches case
articles.description: Manchester City have until Friday to lodge an appeal against the guilty verdict handed down in their case with the Premier League and have stated publicly they intend to do so.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティ、プレミアリーグ違反問題での有罪判決に対し控訴へ
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティは、プレミアリーグの規約違反問題で下された有罪判決に対して金曜日までに控訴する必要があり、控訴する意向を公に表明しています。
articles.body:
Manchester City have until Friday to lodge an appeal against the guilty verdict handed down in their case with the Premier League and have stated publicly they intend to do so.

City's guilt in relation to "all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules" between 2009 and 2018 was detailed in a bombshell statement from the Premier League on Tuesday along with an accompanying written judgement from the independent commission which heard the case.

The Premier League said the "issue of sanction will be addressed separately in a further hearing with the independent commission."

In a statement issued on Tuesday, City said they will appeal the verdict.

It read: "Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe."

In a video message sent out to club employees after the publication of the verdict, CEO Ferran Soriano reiterated City's intention to fight on.

"The whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation," Soriano said.

"That the owner's personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi. This is just not true.

"Our lawyers will now file an appeal that sets out that the opinion contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact and is unsafe."

City have the right to appeal under Premier League rules, although the competition's statement on Tuesday made clear that they want a quick resolution after initially announcing charges against City in February 2023.

"The club has the right to appeal the independent Commission's findings and has until Friday, October 2 to exercise that right," the Premier League said in their lengthy statement on Tuesday. "The Premier League Board's intention is that the full process (including any appeals and publication of relevant decisions) is concluded as soon as possible."

articles.descriptionJa: ジャスティン・ハーバートとドレイク・メイに危険信号？さらなるQBトレードの動き？49ersとパンサーズで募る負傷への懸念？第4週の最新情報をお届けします。
articles.body:
We're onto Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season, and insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been making calls to sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

Drake Maye and the Patriots had an ugly game Sunday, but Maye is hardly the only quarterback with a concerning start to the season. Dan and Jeremy asked around the league to get a sense of which QBs land on the early-season panic meter. And after J.J. McCarthy kicked off trading season Monday in going to the Giants, our insiders poked around on more QB trades that could be on deck. Any other passers potentially switching teams?

Additionally, is the league buying the 3-0 start from the Raiders, who have already matched their win total from 2025? Can Las Vegas keep this up? And which teams -- 3-0 or otherwise -- are getting hit particularly hard with injuries? It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 4.

Jump to:

QB panic meter | QB trades

Raiders' start | Injury impact

Fantasy football advice

Which QB currently sits atop the league's panic meter?

Fowler: Three come to mind here -- Drake Maye, Cam Ward and Justin Herbert. All three garner varying degrees of panic, but I'm putting Maye on top for now. The Year 3 regression is startling. He looks shaken right now. Mike Vrabel's comment after the 35-6 loss to Jacksonville was blunt: "My concern level is very high for this football team." Maye is a big part of that after six interceptions in three games. The next day, Vrabel questioned whether the Patriots' offense needs to scale back its game plans a bit, essentially to do less but do it better.

Still, the notion that Maye's play can improve is there. He was considered one of the cleanest quarterback prospects of the past half-decade when he entered the 2024 draft. He played at an MVP level less than a calendar year ago. And to be sure, the Patriots have not played well around Maye and have not adequately protected him, and wide receiver A.J. Brown's absence is deeply felt. The passing game was designed to feed him the ball often. Josh McDaniels' scheme is also considered to be complex for young passers.

But dating to last year's playoffs, Maye's seven-game production line is 120-of-200 passing for 1,413 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Those are 1970s QB numbers -- and jarring for a quarterback seemingly on the door of superstardom (to be fair, four of those seven were playoff games against top-shelf defenses).

So, I'm leaving the door open for Maye to fix it, but the panic can be found in Vrabel's voice right now. I mean, this team was in the Super Bowl last season, so the expectations couldn't have been higher. Perhaps last season's soft schedule masked a quarterback who was still very much in development.

articles.headline: Ex-Man City chairman calls for club's directors to resign after Premier League guilty verdict
articles.description: Former Manchester City chairman David Bernstein has called for the club's directors to step down after City were found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules.
articles.headlineJa: マンC元会長、プレミアリーグの有罪判決を受けクラブ役員の辞任を要求
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティがプレミアリーグの財務ルールに対する重大な違反で有罪と判断されたことを受け、同クラブの元会長デビッド・バーンスタイン氏は取締役陣の辞任を求めました。
articles.body:
Former Manchester City chairman David Bernstein has called for the club's directors to step down after City were found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules.

The league announced in a statement on Tuesday that City had been found guilty on all charges related to the period between 2009 and 2018, with league CEO Richard Masters saying that the club "systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade."

City said in a statement on Tuesday that they will appeal the verdict.

"I can't think of a penalty strong enough for this, really. I mean, this is absolutely terrible," Bernstein, who was chairman of the club between 1998 and 2003, told talkSPORT.

"I want to raise another question, and that is the position of the board of directors. Because the directors of the club, including the chief executive, who's been there for years and went through this period, are responsible for the running of the club in every respect.

"If this was a public company of some sort, I think the directors, with something as serious as this, would have to stand down or be suspended pending the outcome of all this ... Appeal or no appeal.

"I don't think the present management can credibly continue."

Asked in a separate interview with the BBC whether City's actions constituted fraud, Bernstein suggested that he felt the actions of the board merited a legal investigation.

"I would go that far, yes," he said. "And if it is, -- I'm not a lawyer, and I'm only just putting this on the table as a thought, really -- but it is something that is so serious that it goes beyond the football authorities. It is damning beyond belief.

Bernstein, who is a lifelong City fan, also suggested that the club should be removed from the Premier League.

- Man City to appeal guilty verdict in Premier League breaches case

- Man City should be stripped of titles - Jamie Carragher

- Man City CEO says Premier League verdict part of 'conspiracy'

"If [City's appeal] drags on for a year or two, heaven forbid, that would be the worst thing for everybody," he told talkSPORT.

"But if it did, then you'd have a different situation. So it's a little difficult to predict. But all I would say is that money [a financial penalty] is not sufficient now.

"But if these charges stand now and let's say the appeal does not happen or fails, then I'm afraid for the club I love that they've got to come out of the Premier League. This is beyond awful."

articles.headline: Case Keenum or Tyson Bagent? Bears face a QB decision
articles.description: Keenum stepped up in a big way against the Eagles, but Bagent is healthy and Ben Johnson won't reveal his QB1.
articles.headlineJa: ケース・キーナムかタイソン・ベージェントか？ベアーズがQBの決断を迫られる
articles.descriptionJa: キーナムはイーグルス戦で素晴らしい活躍を見せたが、ベージェントは健康な状態にあり、ベン・ジョンソンは誰が先発QBかを明かしていない。
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- Chicago Bears quarterback Case Keenum had about 30 minutes Monday night before the euphoria of leading a huge win over the Philadelphia Eagles met the reality of possibly heading back to the bench next week. It's a reality with which he is not unfamiliar.

"We'll have a discussion as a coaching staff, and we'll see where we need to go from here," Bears coach Ben Johnson said after the 27-7 win. "But I said it last week, and I'll say it again, there was a reason why Tyson [Bagent] ended training camp as our No. 2 quarterback."

Bagent had spent much of last week in concussion protocol and was active and on the sideline Monday. Caleb Williams was ruled out Saturday because of a hamstring injury.

So Keenum, who hadn't started a regular-season in 1,009 days, stole the spotlight, completing 24-of-34 passes for 247 yards and two touchdowns.

Now he might be in a backup role once again when the Bears host the New York Jets on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, Fox).

In 2017, Keenum subbed in for Sam Bradford with the Minnesota Vikings after a recurring knee injury derailed Bradford after Week 1. Keenum went 11-3 in the regular season, and his game-winning TD pass to Stefon Diggs against the New Orleans Saints in the divisional playoff game is known as the Minneapolis Miracle. The Vikings lost to the Eagles in the NFC Championship Game.

But even as the wins piled up that season, including an eight-game win streak, Keenum knew he was a game away from being back on the bench. Former Vikings coach Mike Zimmer was reluctant to name Keenum the team's full-time starter. He took it game by game and often delayed naming a starter until days before kickoff.

Keenum learned to live with the uncertainty. As he's bounced from backup to starter to backup over his 15-year NFL career, he's learned to appreciate every opportunity.

"This means a bunch to me, man," Keenum told his teammates postgame. "This was taken from me a lot of times. "And to have [Johnson] call me and bring me back, [helped me] find the love of the game again. To have my family, my kids get to watch me ... I'm telling you, we've got something special here." The Bears' win over the Eagles didn't require a miracle from Keenum. The 38-year-old quarterback was "extraordinary" in the eyes of Johnson, completing 71% of his passes for 247 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. He was not sacked and converted a quarterback sneak for a touchdown.

The impact of Keenum's night is more than just a feel-good story. It's the type of performance that may give the Bears the best chance to continue to find wins while Williams works his way back. He is expected to be sidelined three to four weeks with a Grade 2 hamstring strain.

articles.headline: Raphinha returns to Barcelona after injury on Brazil duty
articles.description: Raphinha will return to Barcelona after suffering a thigh injury in Brazil's 4-2 friendly win over Australia on Tuesday.
articles.headlineJa: ハフィーニャ、ブラジル代表活動での負傷によりバルセロナに復帰
articles.descriptionJa: ハフィーニャは火曜日に行われブラジルが4-2で勝利したオーストラリアとの親善試合で太ももを負傷し、バルセロナへ戻ることになった。
articles.body:
Raphinha will return to Barcelona after suffering a thigh injury in Brazil's 4-2 friendly win over Australia on Tuesday.

The Brazilian Football Confederation [CBF] have confirmed the in-form forward will not feature against India on Saturday to allow him to travel back to Europe.

Club sources at Barça said Raphinha will have further tests upon his arrival back in Spain, but the injury is not initially thought to be serious.

"On Wednesday, Raphinha underwent tests that revealed a minor muscle edema in the back of his right thigh," the CBF said.

"As a precaution, and to ensure a speedy recovery, the player will be released from the Brazilian national team, with no replacement called up in his place."

Barça will manage the situation with caution given the injury is in an area where Raphinha experienced a lot of problems last season.

He missed 25 games for club and country in 2025-26 with various hamstring injuries in his right leg.

Converted into a No.9 this season by Barça coach Hansi Flick, Raphinha has started the new campaign in fine form, netting 14 goals in eight appearances in all competitions for his club.

Barça's next game is against Getafe at Spotify Camp Nou in LaLiga on Oct. 10, with matches to follow against Galatasaray, Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, among others, in a hectic October.

articles.headline: Man City's Elliot Anderson no handball call was correct - PL panel
articles.description: The referee and VAR were correct to rule that Manchester City's Elliot Anderson did not handle the ball against Sunderland, a Premier League panel ruled.
articles.headlineJa: マン・シティのエリオット・アンダーソンにハンドを取らなかった判定は正当、PLパネルが結論
articles.descriptionJa: プレミアリーグのパネルは、サンダーランド戦でマンチェスター・シティのエリオット・アンダーソンがハンドを犯さなかったとした主審とVARの判定は正しかったと判定した。
articles.body:
Referee Rob Jones and VAR Michael Salisbury were correct to rule that Manchester City midfielder Elliot Anderson did not handle the ball in his side's thrilling 5-3 win over Sunderland, according to a Premier League panel.

The Black Cats were furious after the ball hit Anderson's hand as he challenged Enzo Le Fée in the City penalty area during a breathless second half.

Jones waved away protests and Salisbury did not overrule him from Stockley Park, which angered Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris.

However, Premier League's Key Match Incidents five-person panel agreed with the on-field decision by a majority of three to two.

Two people on the panel made up of three former players and coaches, a Premier League representative and one from Pro Ref felt that Anderson deliberately moved his arm towards the ball.

The panel's findings read: "The referee's call of no penalty for a potential handball offence against Anderson was supported, 3:2.

"Both players were engaged and the ball was bouncing at close proximity after deflecting off Le Fee.

"Two panellists felt that there was a deliberate secondary movement of the arm from Anderson that was a handball offence."

The panel also voted four to one in ruling VAR's decision not to intervene as correct.

There was also a split decision over Everton's disallowed goal in their 1-0 win over Ipswich at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

- Man City to appeal guilty verdict in Premier League breaches case

- Thomas Tuchel 'did not talk' to England's Man City players about guilty verdict

- Roy Keane: I'd put Man City medals 'in the bin' after 'cheating'

The Toffees thought they had doubled their lead when Thierno Barry headed home, but referee Stuart Attwell was advised Brennan Johnson was offside in front of goalkeeper Christian Walton.

The ruling read: "The VAR intervention to disallow the goal for interfering with an opponent by Johnson was supported, 3:2.

"Johnson was clearly in an offside position, in very close proximity to the goalkeeper and makes a movement, impacting the goalkeeper's ability to set and move to the ball. Two panellists felt that Johnson's position and actions did not impact goalkeeper Walton."

articles.headline: Barcelona chief explains how Lautaro Martínez pursuit ended over a phone call
articles.description: Joan Laporta has confirmed Barcelona tried to sign Lautaro Martínez this summer but quickly gave up once it became apparent Inter Milan would not allow the striker to leave.
articles.headlineJa: バルサ会長、ラウタロ・マルティネス獲得の試みが1本の電話で終了した経緯を明かす
articles.descriptionJa: ジョアン・ラポルタ会長は、バルセロナが今夏ラウタロ・マルティネスの獲得を試みたものの、インテル・ミラノが同ストライカーの放出を認めないことが明確になり、即座に断念したことを認めた。
articles.body:
Joan Laporta has confirmed Barcelona tried to sign Lautaro Martínez this summer but quickly gave up once it became apparent Inter Milan would not allow the striker to leave.

The Spanish champions spent the transfer window trying to sign a No.9, turning their attention to Martínez after failing to land Atlético Madrid's Julián Álvarez.

However, after reaching out to Inter CEO Giuseppe Marotta, Laporta realised a deal for the Argentina international would not be possible either, with Barça eventually signing Gabriel Jesus from Arsenal.

"One day I called Marotta," the Barça chief told Corriere della Sera. "It was he and I on the call -- no intermediaries -- and I told him I would have loved to have Lautaro on my team because I admire the guy so much.

"But Marotta didn't even let me finish speaking. He made it clear Lautaro wasn't for sale and that it wouldn't be up to the player to decide whether or not to move. So I stopped the whole line of thought. There was no way to take it any further."

Following the departures of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres in the post-season, Barça were keen to bolster their attack with a new striker.

But despite signing Jesus on the final day of the transfer window, the solution has come in-house, with Raphinha being converted into a No.9 at the start of the new campaign.

The Brazil forward has quickly adapted to his new position, scoring 14 goals in eight appearances, including back-to-back LaLiga hat tricks before the international break.

It is not the first time Barça have tried to sign Martínez, who was also a target in 2020 when they were looking to replace Luis Suárez.

- Barcelona await updates after Brazil's Raphinha substituted due to thigh discomfort

- Kylian Mbappé, Ibrahima Konaté, Fede Valverde expected to be available for El Clásico - source

- Espanyol sporting director apologises for backing Lamine Yamal to win Ballon d'Or

Speaking earlier in September, Martínez said it was an "honour and a source of immense satisfaction" to be linked to clubs like Barça, but pledged his future to Inter. 

Martínez, who has four goals in four Serie A games this season, has a contract with the club until 2029.

Since signing for the Italian giants from Racing Club in 2018, he has netted 179 goals in 381 appearances, winning three Scudettos, three Coppas Italia and reaching two Champions League finals.
